abstract_research_topics.justification: Game theory is a theoretical framework for understanding social situations among competing players and offers models for decision-making. Its exploration in deep learning is typically more abstract, focusing on the foundational concepts rather than direct applications.

Auxiliary objectives refer to additional goals integrated into deep learning models to improve learning efficiency and performance. This domain focuses on the theoretical considerations of enhancing model architectures and learning processes.

Intrinsic motivation in deep learning explores the conceptual framework that drives agents to engage in tasks out of interest or internal satisfaction. It is primarily an abstract research topic because it focuses on foundational motivational theory rather than specific applications.

This domain involves the theoretical development of models to optimize the internal rewards mechanism in learning agents. It is primarily abstract as it deals with the conceptual framework of learning and behavior modeling.

Catastrophic forgetting examines the theoretical challenges where neural networks forget previously learned information upon learning new information. This is a key theoretical issue in continuous learning and model adaptation.

These models integrate external memory resources and focus on the abstract research of incorporating memory mechanisms into neural networks, aiming to significantly advance theoretical understanding of memory in AI systems.

A mathematical framework used in machine learning to study kernel methods. Its discussion in deep learning is often abstract, dealing with the theoretical aspects of function spaces and kernel representations.

Density estimation entails theoretical methods to estimate the probability distribution of data. In the context of deep learning, it involves exploring statistical modeling and inference, which are abstract topics.

3D equivariance is the theoretical study of algorithms that remain consistent under 3D transformations. It is an abstract topic focusing on the mathematical and theoretical foundations of symmetrical transformations in neural network design.

application_domains.justification: Game playing represents applying deep learning to create strategies and behaviors in gaming environments. It is a practical application domain, focusing on real-world use of AI.

Auxiliary tasks are practical implementations of deep learning whereby models learn supplementary tasks to improve performance on primary tasks. This involves applying abstract concepts to real scenarios.
Experience replay is used in reinforcement learning applications to improve learning efficiency by reusing past experiences. It represents a real-world technique applied in practical AI systems.
In an application context, forgetting refers to the practical ways neural networks lose information over time, often requiring solutions to mitigate its impact on real-world applications.

Long-term memory in AI refers to how systems are designed to retain and recall information over extended periods, a practical aspect heavily applied in the development of more advanced cognitive systems.
Memory systems in deep learning applications deal with how information is stored and accessed in models. It is often focused on improving practical implementations of AI systems.
Working memory in AI involves the application of techniques that allow systems to handle short-term tasks and information, crucial for real-time processing in many AI applications.

This involves the practical application of linear quadratic control systems with Gaussian processes, serving as an application in systems control, robotics, and similar fields.
While based on an abstract concept, 3D rotational equivariance is practically applied to allow neural networks to recognize and process rotations in 3D spaces for applications like vision processing.

In applications, equivariance enables neural networks to maintain consistent performance amid various transformations, utilized in fields such as image and signal processing.
This domain applies equivarient principles practically to design models that remain invariant under certain transformations, critical for applications in computer vision and graphics.

These networks find practical application in scenarios requiring performance consistency under symmetrical input transformations, a practical domain for many technologies reliant on geometry and symmetry.
